nina.docs: I opened a docs PR adding a compact 'HSM migration quicknotes' appendix for Private/VPC installs. It includes a config diff (managed KMS -> pkcs11), a short pkcs11 path example, and a tiny Python conn-check for semi-airgapped sites. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4923
alex.eng: Nice. Can you make the config diff minimal and avoid any real hostnames or secrets? Also add a note about doing key-wrap rotation only after testing on a staging HSM.
tim.sre: From SRE: include a short checklist for networking gotchas on baremetal (MTU mismatch, NAT hairpin) and a minimal egress CIDR example for conn-checks. Example CIDRs we use in staging: 203.0.113.0/24:443, 198.51.100.0/24:443.
rachel.sec: Security asks to explicitly warn against checking in any private keys or literal credentials. Also add a line about least-privilege operator accounts and auditing role mappings on the HSM.
nina.docs: Will do. Here's the minimal config diff I plan to include (no secrets):
```diff
- kms:
-   type: managed
-   endpoint: https://kms-managed.example
+ kms:
+   type: pkcs11
+   pkcs11_module: /opt/hsm/lib/libpkcs11.so
+   slot: 0
+   label: redwood-kms
```
alex.eng: Good. For pkcs11 path wording use "configure pkcs11 plugin path via the KMS connector" instead of "open pkcs11". Add an example systemd drop-in for when the module sits on an external mount.
tim.sre: Drop-in suggestion:
```
[Service]
Environment=PKCS11_MODULE=/opt/hsm/lib/libpkcs11.so
Restart=on-failure
After=local-fs.target network.target
```
rachel.sec: Also add a brief migration note: export current key-wrap metadata from managed KMS, validate export on a staging HSM, then import and rotate. Warn: do not rotate in peak windows and ensure HSM policies are backed up.
